Release a component without a market: a release is a Git tag, pushed to the component's own repository.

The version is metadata.version in component.yaml — the single source of truth. Only component.yaml is read;
a brickkit.yaml in the same directory (the author's local workbench) plays no part.

Before anything is written, every check must pass:
  - component.yaml parses and validates
  - the component directory has no uncommitted changes (for a component in a subdirectory of a monorepo,
    only its own directory counts)
  - the branch has an upstream and nothing unpushed: the tagged commit must already be in the remote history
  - the tag does not exist yet, locally or on the remote
Then the tag is created and pushed. If the push fails, the local tag is deleted again — a release either
happens completely or leaves no trace.

The tag is <version> when the component directory is the repository root, and <scope>-<name>/<version>
when it is a subdirectory — the names the git install source reads.

--local releases every component in the project's local install sources: all of them are checked first,
then tagged and pushed one by one. One already released (its tag is on the current commit) is skipped;
at the first push failure it stops — earlier releases stay, later ones are not attempted.

brickkit publish (to a market) is a separate command.

Usage:
  brickkit release [flags]

Examples:
  brickkit release                                  the component in the current directory
  brickkit release --path ./components/erp/backend
  brickkit release --path svc/api                   a component in a monorepo subdirectory (tag erp-api/<version>)
  brickkit release --local                          every local-source component of the project

Flags:
  -h, --help          help for release
      --local         Release every component in the project's local install sources
      --path string   The component directory (where component.yaml is) (default ".")

Global Flags:
      --log-level string   Level of the JSON logs on stderr (debug | info | warn | error | off) (default "off")
